why:
phase-492 W1.b: renamed from `rclc_service_callback_t`, which is rclc's name for a different contract (a deserialised message, no context); RFC-0089 rule 2 gives this one a distinct name.

RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-18 (phase-417 W5.e follow-through), divergence -> extension. Both halves of the old one-line reason were false, and they are recorded here rather than smoothed away.

It said: "bound to the entity at creation; see the pubsub stage's `c:subscription_callback_t`."

(1) THE BINDING SITE MOVED. phase-417 stage 6 took the callback off `*_init` and put it at registration -- `rclc_executor_add_service_raw(exec, svc, cb, ctx)`, which is where rclc supplies it (`rclc_executor_add_service`). The sentence described an arrangement the tree no longer has. (2) THE ROW IT DEFERRED TO NO LONGER SAYS THAT EITHER: `c:subscription_callback_t` was itself re-verdicted divergence -> extension on 2026-09-13, so a `see` pointing at it was inheriting a retracted argument.

WHAT THE DIFFERENCE ACTUALLY IS: the DATA contract, plus a return. Ours is `bool (*)(const uint8_t *request, size_t request_len, uint8_t *response, size_t response_capacity, size_t *response_len, void *context)` -- CDR bytes both ways -- where rclc's `rclc_service_callback_with_context_t` is `void (*)(const void *request, void *response, void *context)` over DESERIALIZED payloads. The `bool` is not decoration: `srv_raw_try_process` sends a reply only on `ok && resp_len > 0` (`executor/arena.rs`), so returning `false` is how a handler refuses to put a malformed or oversized reply on the wire. rclc's `void` callback cannot refuse at all.

Extension rather than divergence, because the faithful counterpart now SHIPS beside it and carries the correspondence: `packs/c/service.h.jinja` emits `<Srv>_handler_fn_t = void (*)(const <Srv>_request *, <Srv>_response *, void *)` -- rclc's three parameters in rclc's order, with the two payload pointers TYPED -- and the generated trampoline `<Srv>_service_handle_request` is an `rclc_service_callback_t` that owns the CDR on both sides. Until W5.e's callers landed (2026-09-18) this byte callback was the only delivery shape and so stood in for rclc's typed one; it is now the byte TIER beside a faithful one, which is where a caller doing its own CDR or FORWARDING a payload belongs.

NOTE WHAT DOES NOT APPEAR HERE: "no allocator". Neither side allocates -- rclc makes the caller own `request_msg` / `response_msg`, and ours puts both structs in the caller's `<Srv>_service_handler_t`.
